newsitem.title: UK: Spain targets first single currency group-FT.
newsitem.headline: Spain targets first single currency group-FT.

text.p: Spanish prime minister Jose Maria Aznar has said Spain will be among the first group of single currency nations in Europe, the Financial Times reported on Monday.

"We will be there," Aznar told the newspaper in an interview. "I am ready to take whatever measures are necessary to succeed, because I am absolutely persuaded that Spain is staking its stability and prosperity in this bet," the paper quoted him as saying.
It said Aznar believed the goal of meeting essential requirements on inflation and public finances by the end of 1997 and then joining the Euro currency in January 1999 had popular support.

"And in the second place, it is playing politically for the most important membership there is. Also, I am very convinced that this has the backing of the majority of Spanish opinion," he told the newspaper.
Aznar said his minority Popular Party (PP) government's budget, unveiled last Friday, was "very tough".

The prime minister also said he was not interested in altering the criteria or the timetable for a European single currency, a message he apparently gave to his Italian counterpart Romani Prodi two weeks ago when the two met in Valencia.
"He (Prodi) wanted Spain and Italy to walk together holding hands towards Maastricht...I am not interested in holding hands. I told him we'd be there, right at the start," Aznar said.
"Spain is very conscious of the political nature of the decision (on who joins) but is absolutely determined about fulfilment of the conditions."

The FT said Spain was attempting to roughly match France's performance. "The closer I am to France, the happier I will be," Aznar told the paper. While saying it would not be a disaster if Spain's entry was delayed, he stressed it would be better if it made it from the outset.

On the subject of the budget, Aznar told the FT that Spain's mentality and credibility were changing. "I think one of the elements in the modernisation of Spain is changing the mentality about spending...I have taken on this responsibility and this engagement," he said.

The FT said Aznar predicted this year would see a fall of 200,000 in the number of unemployed. He also said year-on-year growth in inflation adjusted gross domestic product could recover to a 2.3 percent rate at the end of the year and three percent in 1997.
